@ a receiver under .down~(4) runs at the frames 0 4 8 and sees the events of the frames before it, all of them: an event at the frame of a tick comes at the next tick
@ a receiver under .up~(2) gets the event of its frame before its first run: both runs see the sum up to the frame, and sample_tick() is 2 p + j
@ at a frame where a maker of sample / 2 and a maker of sample both give an event, the first comes first: the reset by the first is before the add of the second
@ a flow that gives the event it gets, under .down~(4) or .up~(2), gives it once: the sums are those of the call with no chain
@ a head with a gathered input and an event input under .down~(4): the window is the four frames before the tick, the events are all those before the tick
@ a reset by an event between two ticks: inside the boundary it puts back the part only, outside it puts back the ring of the window too
@ a reset by an event at the frame of a tick comes after the tick: the part is back for the next tick, and the ring written from the frame of the event is kept
@ when~ and .down~(2) in either order read the level at the ticks; a reset by an event reaches the output the when~ holds only where the when~ is inside it
@ a receiver of events under .down~(4) and when~ of the level of an event, in either order: the part is stopped between runs but the events are still taken

@ a part under .up~(2) with a when~ of an event: the bundle of a stopped frame is two copies of the last output; a reset by an event at a stopped frame puts it back only if the reset is outside the when~
@ an event between the boundary that deals and the .up~ that goes past it puts back the ring and the dealt array only when it is outside the boundary, before the first run of its frame
process 1 params k=7 frames=3 in r=[0 1 0]
